claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Your son Alex is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK, which is a good start.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care, meaning you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for all of Alex's day-to-day needs - his food, clothes, school things, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency status:

**Do you live in the UK? And if so, what is your immigration or residency status? For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're here in England. I'm a UK citizen, so no immigration issues or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a few more questions to make sure I have the complete picture:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation for an extended period? Or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex is in hospital at the moment. He's abroad - we had to take him overseas for treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. This is an important detail that could affect your eligibility.

**How long has Alex been in hospital abroad, and do you regularly spend money on him while he's there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about some of those details to be honest. He went abroad for the hospital treatment, but I can't say for certain about all the specifics of the situation or whether I've been able to keep up with spending on him regularly while he's been there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - this is a complex situation and you're dealing with a lot.

Let me ask one clarifying question to help me assess this properly:

**Do you know approximately how long Alex has been in the hospital abroad - for example, has it been less than 12 weeks, more than 12 weeks, or are you unsure of the timeframe?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure of the exact timeframe, to be honest. It's been difficult to keep track of everything with all that's been going on.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this must be a very difficult time for you.

Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

You've told me that:
- Alex is 8 years old and normally lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for all his day-to-day needs
- You're a UK citizen living in England
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is currently in hospital abroad for treatment
- You're unsure of the exact timeframe he's been there and uncertain about whether you've been regularly spending money on him

The rules state that Child Benefit can be affected if a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks. There is an exception for children in hospital abroad - you may still be entitled if the child only went abroad to be in hospital, you're back in the UK, and you regularly spend money on them.

However, since you don't have sufficient information about:
- How long Alex has been in hospital abroad
- Whether you've been able to regularly spend money on him during this time

I cannot make a definite determination of your eligibility. This situation falls outside what I can definitively assess with the information available.
